pages.api:
# API

> Topics, the HTTP surface and the store vector.

## Input

`iq.cs16/<source>` (`iq.cs16.v1`, stream), read with the `drop-oldest` policy: if the cog falls behind, records are overwritten and the missing samples are counted as `samples_skipped`.

## Output

`spectrum.psd/<source>` (`spectrum.psd.v1`, reading) every window; `band.occupancy/<source>` (`telemetry.v1`, reading) every interval, one per band.

## HTTP (loopback)

`/status`, `/raw` (the newest spectrum reading), `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Store vector (id 30)

`[centre GHz, rate MS/s, occupancy overall, floor dBFS, peak dBFS, loss fraction, windows published, uncalibrated]`.
pages.readings:
# Readings

> What the two readings contain and how to read them.

## `spectrum.psd/<source>` (`spectrum.psd.v1`)

The registered reading: `center_hz`, `span_hz` (the sample rate, the whole width the bins cover), and `bins`, 256 values in dBFS from the lowest frequency to the highest, rounded to 0.1 dB. The analog filter rolls off at the edges, so the usable part is the middle `bandwidth_hz / sample_rate_hz` of the bins. A full-scale complex tone in one FFT bin reads 0 dBFS.

Added fields: `bandwidth_hz`, `fft_size` (1024), `frames` averaged, `integration_ms`, `floor_dbfs` (median level), `peak_dbfs`, `uncalibrated`, and the loss counts: `samples_used`, `samples_lost`, `samples_skipped`, `samples_dead`, `loss_fraction`.

## `band.occupancy/<source>` (`telemetry.v1`)

One reading per band per minute, as named items. `band.centre`, `band.rate`, `band.bandwidth` say which band. `occ.overall` and `occ.slice0` to `occ.slice7` are the busy share overall and in eight equal slices of the usable band (0 to 1). `floor` and `peak` are the mean median level and the highest bin in dBFS. `occ.threshold` is the busy threshold above the floor (10 dB).

`coverage` is the share of the minute the radio spent on this band. When the owner takes turns between bands, each band's reading covers only its own dwells, and `coverage` shows how much. `samples.*` and `loss.fraction` are the loss accounting for the minute.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it after the owner, point it at the owner's source name.

```
cog-spectrum --once --simulate                  # synthetic band, prints one report
cog-spectrum --once --replay cap.iq             # analyse a capture from sdr-pluto-rx --record
cog-spectrum --source venq-pluto                # live, from the node's cogbus
cog-spectrum --ask-plan 2437e6:5e6:5000         # also ask the owner to include this band
```

Live mode needs `WEFTOS_COGBUS` and `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN` and a cog manifest that lists `iq.cs16` as an input. The source name is the owner's `--service` (default `venq-pluto`). The cog reconnects and resubscribes when the broker or the owner restarts.

`--ask-plan` sends a `plan` call to `svc.sdr` so the owner visits a band for this cog; with no owner plans of other consumers it simply runs that band. Otherwise the cog analyses whatever the owner is tuned to.

Windows are 2 s (`--psd-secs`), occupancy intervals 60 s (`--occ-secs`), the threshold 10 dB (`--thresh-db`). `/status`, `/raw` (the newest spectrum), `/guide` and `/healthz` are on `127.0.0.1:8064`.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Turn the radio's samples into a spectrum and a busy-or-quiet figure per band, and say how much was lost on the way.

`spectrum` reads the IQ stream that `sdr-pluto-rx` publishes. It never opens the radio. Every couple of seconds it publishes a power spectrum (`spectrum.psd`), and every minute a band occupancy reading (`band.occupancy`) for each band the radio visited.

## The short path

1. **Start the owner.** `sdr-pluto-rx` must be running and streaming. → see **Set up**
2. **Start this cog.** It subscribes to the owner's stream and waits for it if it is not up yet.
3. **Read the occupancy.** `occ.overall` is the share of time-frequency cells more than 10 dB above the noise floor. → see **Readings**
4. **Read the loss.** `loss.fraction` and `samples.lost` say how much of the stream never reached the spectrum. → see **Troubleshoot**

You can try it with no radio: `--once --simulate` makes a synthetic band marked `SYNTHETIC`, and `--once --replay FILE` analyses a capture made with the owner's `--record`.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- Occupancy is relative to the noise floor of each frame, not an absolute level. A band that is wall to wall busy has no floor to measure against and reads low.
- Levels are dBFS of the 12-bit converter, not dBm. They are uncalibrated outside 325 to 3800 MHz and are marked so.
- Samples the owner lost, samples this cog missed, and samples from a dead receive path are counted apart and left out of the spectrum. A spectrum built from a stream that lost 30 percent says so in the same message.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> The loss counters tell you where samples went.

| Symptom | Likely cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `waiting`, no records | The owner is not running or not streaming. Start `sdr-pluto-rx` and check its `/healthz`. |
| `samples.lost` rising | The owner lost samples on the radio link (USB 2.0 tops out near 7.5 MS/s). Lower the rate. |
| `samples.skipped` rising | This cog fell behind the ring and records were overwritten. Check the load; the FFT needs about a tenth of a core at 5 MS/s. |
| `samples.dead` rising | The receive path delivers zeros. See the owner's guide: loopback or a loose cable. |
| occupancy reads 0 on a busy band | There is no quiet part to measure the floor against. Occupancy is relative; use the spectrum and `peak`. |
| `uncalibrated` is 1 | The band is outside the chip's rated 325 to 3800 MHz. Shapes are right, levels are not. |

toml:
# Sensor guide for spectrum (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# The cog reads another cog's IQ stream, so there is no wiring: the only diagram is the signal flow.

schema = 1
title = "Spectrum and band occupancy from the PlutoSDR stream"
sensor = "iq.cs16.v1 stream from the sdr-pluto-rx cog (PlutoSDR Nano)"
cog = "spectrum"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "readings", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
owner_running = "setup"
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
export = "setup"
spectrum = "readings"
occupancy = "readings"
loss = "troubleshoot"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "sdr-pluto-rx"
detail = "iq.cs16.v1 ring, loss counted"

[[flow]]
name = "Welch FFT"
detail = "1024 points, Hann, 50% overlap"

[[flow]]
name = "Noise floor"
detail = "median bin per frame, +10 dB = busy"

[[flow]]
name = "spectrum cog"
detail = "PSD each window, occupancy each minute"

[[flow]]
name = "Outputs"
detail = "spectrum.psd, band.occupancy, :8064"
